```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2026_timolol"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2026_timolol"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70334> (open access; supplement
  `psp4.70334-sup-0001`)

Li et al. (2026) pooled three Chinese registration trials of a 0.5% timolol
maleate gel developed for superficial infantile hemangioma: a phase I study in
healthy adults (CTR20191402), a phase Ib/II dose-escalation study in infants
(CTR20202613), and a randomized, placebo-controlled phase III study in infants
(CTR20221992). The final model is one-compartment with first-order absorption
and elimination, allometric body-weight scaling with fixed exponents (0.75 on
CL/F, 1 on Vc/F, reference 60 kg), a relative bioavailability fixed to 1 in
adults and estimated separately for each infant trial (252 and 202), IIV on CL/F
only, and a proportional residual error. No covariate was retained beyond
weight.

# Population

The analysis included 810 concentrations from 138 subjects: 478 from 24 healthy
adults (16 male, 8 female; mean age 28.1 years, mean weight 60.4 kg; Table S3)
and 332 from 114 infants with proliferative superficial infantile hemangioma
(44 male, 70 female; mean age 2.98 months, range 1.2-6.0; mean weight 6.24 kg,
range 3.50-9.57; Table S4). Infants were enrolled in the phase Ib/II study
(n = 35) and the phase III study (n = 79). The median baseline lesion area was
1.5 cm^2 (range 0.04-15.5). Concentrations were measured in dried blood spots
by LC-MS/MS (LLOQ 0.0500 ng/mL).

The gel was applied at a nominal 3 mg of gel per cm^2 per application. Adults
covered 10% of body surface area (about 4.8 g of gel per application); infants
treated the lesion. Dosing regimens (Table S1):

| Study | Regimen |
|---|---|
| Phase I, adults | Single dose on day 1; then twice (cohort 1, days 5-10), four times or six times daily (cohorts 2 and 3, days 10-15); single dose on day 11 or day 16 |
| Phase Ib/II, infants | Single dose on day 1; then twice, three times or five times daily for 6 days; single dose on day 11 |
| Phase III, infants | Three times daily for 24 weeks |

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Li_2026_timolol")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lka` | log(0.01) 1/h | Table 1, 'Ka, h-1' = 0.01 (RSE 4.3%) |
| `lcl` | log(3030 x 10^3) L/h | Table 1, 'CL/F, x10^3 L/h' = 3030 (RSE 39.4%) |
| `lvc` | log(22,100 x 10^3) L | Table 1, 'Vc/F, x10^3 L' = 22,100 (RSE 21.3%) |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.75 (fixed) | Table 1, 'WT on CL/F' = 0.75 FIX; footnote CL = CLTV x (WT/60)^0.75 |
| `e_wt_vc` | 1 (fixed) | Table 1, 'WT on Vc/F' = 1 FIX; footnote Vc = Vc,TV x (WT/60) |
| `lfdepot` | log(1) (fixed) | Table 1 footnote: F1 in healthy adults fixed to 1 |
| `e_study_ctr20202613_fdepot` | 252 | Table 1, 'F1Ib/II' = 252 (RSE 29.4%) |
| `e_study_ctr20221992_fdepot` | 202 | Table 1, 'F1III' = 202 (RSE 27.9%) |
| `etalcl` | 1.396^2 = 1.949 | Table 1, 'omega (CL), %' = 139.6 (RSE 6.7%); see Assumptions |
| `propSd` | 0.49 | Table 1, 'sigma (Prop), %' = 49.0 (RSE 6.0%) |
| One compartment, first-order absorption and elimination | n/a | Results, Model Development |
| Allometric scaling, reference weight 60 kg | n/a | Methods; Table 1 footnote |
| `Cc = 1000 * central / vc` | n/a | mg/L to ng/mL; concentrations in ng/mL throughout the paper |

# Virtual cohort

The original data are not public. The cohorts below follow the Table S1
schedules with covariates drawn to match Tables S3 and S4. Each dose is the
nominal amount of gel: 4,800 mg per adult application, and 3 mg/cm^2 times the
lesion area per infant application. Lesion areas are drawn from a log-normal
distribution with the Table S4 median (1.5 cm^2) and a spread chosen to
reproduce its mean (3.24 cm^2), truncated to the observed range.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)

rtrunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, mean, sd), lo), hi)
}

# One subject-level covariate table per arm; IDs are offset so that arms can be
# stacked without colliding.
make_subjects <- function(n, arm, population, id_offset) {
  is_adult <- population == "adult"
  tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    arm = arm,
    WT = if (is_adult) {
      rtrunc_norm(n, 60.4, 8.38, 49.4, 76.2)
    } else {
      rtrunc_norm(n, 6.24, 1.10, 3.50, 9.57)
    },
    BHS = if (is_adult) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n, log(1.5), 1.24), 0.04), 15.5)
    },
    amt_app = if (is_adult) 4800 else 3 * BHS,
    STUDY_CTR20202613 = as.integer(population == "phase Ib/II"),
    STUDY_CTR20221992 = as.integer(population == "phase III")
  )
}

# Dose times for the phase I and phase Ib/II design: a single dose at time 0,
# a multiple-dose block of 6 days, and a final single dose.
schedule_times <- function(per_day, block_start_h, last_dose_h) {
  block <- seq(block_start_h, last_dose_h - 1e-6, by = 24 / per_day)
  c(0, block, last_dose_h)
}

build_events <- function(subjects, dose_times, obs_times) {
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(subjects, time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", amt = amt_app)
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(subjects, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    select(-amt_app, -BHS)
}

n_arm <- 100L

arms <- list(
  list(arm = "Adults, twice daily", pop = "adult", per_day = 2, start = 96, last = 240),
  list(arm = "Adults, four times daily", pop = "adult", per_day = 4, start = 216, last = 360),
  list(arm = "Adults, six times daily", pop = "adult", per_day = 6, start = 216, last = 360),
  list(arm = "Infants phase Ib/II, twice daily", pop = "phase Ib/II", per_day = 2, start = 96, last = 240),
  list(arm = "Infants phase Ib/II, three times daily", pop = "phase Ib/II", per_day = 3, start = 96, last = 240),
  list(arm = "Infants phase Ib/II, five times daily", pop = "phase Ib/II", per_day = 5, start = 96, last = 240)
)

events_short <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(arms), function(i) {
  a <- arms[[i]]
  subj <- make_subjects(n_arm, a$arm, a$pop, id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_arm)
  dose_times <- schedule_times(a$per_day, a$start, a$last)
  # Observing at every dose time as well puts a sample on each NCA interval
  # boundary (the five-times-daily interval does not fall on the 2-h grid).
  build_events(
    subj,
    dose_times = dose_times,
    obs_times = sort(unique(c(seq(0, a$last + 240, by = 2), dose_times)))
  )
}))

# Phase III: three times daily for 24 weeks, a dense grid over one steady-state
# dosing interval at week 12 and a daily grid otherwise.
subj_p3 <- make_subjects(200L, "Infants phase III, three times daily", "phase III",
  id_offset = length(arms) * n_arm
)
week12 <- 12 * 7 * 24
events_p3 <- build_events(
  subj_p3,
  dose_times = seq(0, 24 * 7 * 24 - 8, by = 8),
  obs_times = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24 * 7 * 24, by = 24), seq(week12, week12 + 8, by = 0.25))))
)

events <- bind_rows(events_short, events_p3)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[events$evid == 1L, c("id", "time")]))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Li_2026_timolol")
# The default LSODA step budget is occasionally exhausted between sparse
# observations; a larger budget costs nothing when it is not needed.
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("arm", "WT"), maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  as.data.frame()

mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
```

# Replicate Figure 2 (visual predictive check)

The solid lines are the simulated medians and the shaded bands the simulated
5th-95th percentiles. The points are the observed medians of Figure 2, read by
the maintainers from the published plot by eye (approximate to the plot
resolution). The infant panels use the nominal dose described above; see the
next section for why they sit below the published data.

```{r fig2-digitised}
fig2_obs <- tribble(
  ~arm, ~time, ~Cc,
  "Adults, twice daily", 130, 0.035,
  "Adults, twice daily", 180, 0.10,
  "Adults, twice daily", 222, 0.20,
  "Adults, twice daily", 300, 0.14,
  "Adults, four times daily", 250, 0.03,
  "Adults, four times daily", 300, 0.10,
  "Adults, four times daily", 365, 0.30,
  "Adults, four times daily", 450, 0.15,
  "Adults, four times daily", 590, 0.03,
  "Adults, six times daily", 260, 0.05,
  "Adults, six times daily", 340, 0.55,
  "Adults, six times daily", 385, 0.45,
  "Adults, six times daily", 500, 0.12,
  "Adults, six times daily", 590, 0.03,
  "Infants phase Ib/II (all regimens)", 240, 2.0,
  "Infants phase Ib/II (all regimens)", 250, 2.3,
  "Infants phase Ib/II (all regimens)", 265, 1.3,
  "Infants phase Ib/II (all regimens)", 289, 0.95,
  "Infants phase Ib/II (all regimens)", 312, 0.65,
  "Infants phase III, three times daily", 2000, 4.0,
  "Infants phase III, three times daily", 4000, 4.3
)
```

```{r fig2, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 9}
vpc <- sim |>
  mutate(panel = ifelse(grepl("phase Ib/II", arm), "Infants phase Ib/II (all regimens)", arm)) |>
  filter(
    (grepl("Adults, twice", panel) & time >= 100 & time <= 320) |
      (grepl("Adults, (four|six)", panel) & time >= 230 & time <= 600) |
      (grepl("Ib/II", panel) & time >= 240 & time <= 312) |
      (grepl("phase III", panel) & time >= 1000 & time %% 24 == 0)
  ) |>
  group_by(panel, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    p50 = median(Cc),
    p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

panel_levels <- c(
  "Adults, twice daily", "Adults, four times daily", "Adults, six times daily",
  "Infants phase Ib/II (all regimens)", "Infants phase III, three times daily"
)
vpc$panel <- factor(vpc$panel, levels = panel_levels)
fig2_panels <- fig2_obs |>
  rename(panel = arm) |>
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = panel_levels))

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_point(data = fig2_panels, aes(time, Cc), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Timolol concentration (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Li 2026. Points: observed medians read from the figure."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig2-check}
# Adult panels: the simulated median at each digitised time, against the
# digitised observed median. Relative bioavailability is fixed to 1 in adults,
# so this tests CL/F, Vc/F, ka and the dose-unit reading together.
# Each digitised time is matched to the nearest point of the 2-h grid.
sim_median_grid <- sim |>
  filter(grepl("^Adults", arm)) |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(sim_median = median(Cc), .groups = "drop")
adult_cmp <- fig2_obs |>
  filter(grepl("^Adults", arm)) |>
  mutate(time_grid = 2 * round(time / 2)) |>
  left_join(sim_median_grid, by = c("arm", "time_grid" = "time")) |>
  select(-time_grid) |>
  mutate(ratio = sim_median / Cc)
stopifnot(!anyNA(adult_cmp$sim_median))

adult_cmp |>
  rename(
    "Arm" = arm, "Time (h)" = time, "Figure 2 median (ng/mL)" = Cc,
    "Simulated median (ng/mL)" = sim_median, "Simulated / observed" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

# Structural check on the centre of the comparison. A misread x10^3 on CL/F or
# a dose in mg of timolol rather than mg of gel moves every ratio by a factor
# of 200 to 1000; reading error on a log-scale figure is well under 2-fold.
stopifnot(
  abs(log(median(adult_cmp$ratio))) < log(2),
  quantile(abs(log(adult_cmp$ratio)), 0.9) < log(3)
)
```

The adult panels agree to within the reading error of the figure: the median
ratio of simulated to observed is
`r signif(median(adult_cmp$ratio), 2)`.

# Infant exposure at the nominal dose

For a dose of 1 mg of gel three times daily, the typical-value steady-state
average concentration is `F * D / (tau * CL)`. With the phase III relative
bioavailability and the median infant weight this can be checked against the
solve directly; both sides use the same parameters, so the agreement is
numerical.

```{r infant-typical}
p <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
cl_inf <- exp(p[["lcl"]]) * (6.2 / 60)^0.75
cavg_per_mg <- 1000 * p[["e_study_ctr20221992_fdepot"]] * 1 / (8 * cl_inf)

ev_check <- et(amt = 1, ii = 8, addl = 600, cmt = "depot") |>
  et(c(seq(0, 3984, by = 24), seq(4000, 4008, by = 0.05)), cmt = "central")
chk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, ev_check,
  params = c(WT = 6.2, STUDY_CTR20202613 = 0, STUDY_CTR20221992 = 1),
  maxsteps = 1e6
) |> as.data.frame()
cavg_solve <- mean(chk$Cc[chk$time >= 4000])
stopifnot(abs(cavg_solve / cavg_per_mg - 1) < 0.01)

implied_mg_gel <- 4.62 / cavg_per_mg
```

The typical phase III infant reaches `r signif(cavg_per_mg, 3)` ng/mL per mg
of gel per application at steady state. The paper's median empirical-Bayes
Cmax,ss of 4.62 ng/mL (Results) therefore corresponds to about
`r round(implied_mg_gel)` mg of gel per application, whereas 3 mg/cm^2 over the
median 1.5 cm^2 lesion is 4.5 mg and over a 3 cm^2 lesion is the 9 mg the
paper quotes. With the nominal dose, the model predicts infant concentrations
one to two orders of magnitude below the published infant data (Figure 2D and
2E above, and the comparison below), while it reproduces the adult data.

The ratio of infant to adult concentration does not depend on the dose units,
so the mismatch is not a units problem of the packaged model: the dose amounts
the authors recorded for infants are evidently larger than the nominal
3 mg/cm^2 times lesion area (for example, the gel may have been applied beyond
the lesion margin), and the paper does not report them. Users simulating
infants should treat the relative bioavailabilities as tied to the authors'
infant dose records and expect the nominal-dose predictions here to be low.

# PKNCA validation

Steady-state NCA over one 8-hour dosing interval at week 12 for the phase III
arm, and over the last multiple-dose interval for the other arms.

```{r pknca}
last_block_dose <- function(per_day, last) last - 24 / per_day
intervals_tbl <- bind_rows(lapply(arms, function(a) {
  tibble(arm = a$arm, start = last_block_dose(a$per_day, a$last), end = a$last)
})) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(arm = "Infants phase III, three times daily", start = week12, end = week12 + 8)) |>
  mutate(cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, cav = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)

conc_df <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, arm, time, Cc)
dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1L) |>
  select(id, arm, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals_tbl))

nca_res$result |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "cav")) |>
  group_by(arm, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  rename("Arm" = arm, "Cmax,ss (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Cmin,ss (ng/mL)" = cmin, "Cavg,ss (ng/mL)" = cav) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated steady-state exposure per arm (nominal doses).")
```

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tribble(
  ~arm, ~cmax,
  "Infants phase III, three times daily", 4.62
)
p3_res <- nca_res
p3_res$result <- nca_res$result |>
  filter(arm == "Infants phase III, three times daily", PPTESTCD == "cmax")

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = p3_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "arm",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated (nominal dose) vs published median Cmax,ss. * differs by >20%.")

p3_shortfall <- 4.62 / median(p3_res$result$PPORRES)
```

The starred phase III row is the infant dose discrepancy described in the
previous section, not a transcription error: the parameters reproduce the adult
data. The published median is `r round(p3_shortfall)` times the simulated one,
in line with the ratio of the implied application amount
(`r round(implied_mg_gel)` mg) to the nominal amount on the median lesion
(4.5 mg), which is `r round(implied_mg_gel / 4.5)`.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Dose units and the x10^3 scaling of CL/F and Vc/F.** Table 1 lists
  'CL/F, x10^3 L/h' = 3030 and 'Vc/F, x10^3 L' = 22,100. The packaged model
  reads these as 3.03 x 10^6 L/h and 2.21 x 10^7 L, with doses in mg of gel
  applied (not mg of timolol). The paper expresses every dose as an amount of
  gel (4.8 g per adult application, about 9 mg per infant application), and
  this reading reproduces the adult data, where the relative bioavailability is
  fixed to 1: the adult panels of Figure 2 agree within the reading error, and
  a single 4,800 mg adult application gives a typical peak near 0.013 ng/mL,
  consistent with the 83% of post-first-dose adult samples that were below the
  limit of quantification (Table S2). Reading the parameters as 3030 L/h with
  doses in mg of timolol maleate overpredicts the adult data several-fold.
* **IIV scale.** Table 1 reports 'omega (CL), %' = 139.6 with RSE 6.7% and a
  symmetric 95% CI (121-158). The packaged model reads this as the log-scale
  standard deviation (omega = 1.396, variance 1.949) rather than a CV
  (variance log(1 + 1.396^2) = 1.082). An RSE of 6.7% from 138 subjects is
  below what a variance estimate can achieve (about sqrt(2/138) = 12%), and the
  phase III VPC band in Figure 2E (5th-95th percentile spanning roughly 0.35 to
  50 ng/mL around a median near 4 ng/mL) matches a total log-scale SD near 1.5,
  which the SD reading gives and the CV reading does not.
* **Infant doses.** The paper does not report the infant dose amounts used in
  the analysis dataset. This vignette uses 3 mg/cm^2 times a lesion area drawn
  to match Table S4. As discussed above, this underpredicts the infant data by
  one to two orders of magnitude; the parameters were not adjusted.
* **Body weight** is held at its baseline value. Infants in the phase III study
  gain weight over 24 weeks; the paper does not say whether weight was
  time-varying in the analysis.
* **Matrix.** Concentrations were measured in dried blood spots; the paper
  calls them plasma concentrations. The model output is the concentration the
  model was fitted to.
* **Dosing schedule.** The phase I and phase Ib/II schedules are laid out from
  the sampling days in Table S1 (multiple-dose block on days 5-10 or 10-15,
  final single dose on day 11 or 16). The adult arms simulate 100 subjects each
  rather than 8; the phase III arm simulates 200 rather than 79.
* **Observed medians in Figure 2** were read by eye from the published figure.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found in Europe PMC as of
  2026-11-17.
